entries.title: Silverpine Forest
body: A vast, ancient forest of tall silver-barked pines along Lordaeron's rugged western coast, between Tirisfal to the north, Lordamere Lake to the east and the Greymane Wall of Gilneas to the south. It is haunted and wild, and eerily silent; abandoned farmsteads and mines dot the land, home now to the darker denizens of the woods.

The road through Silverpine was once counted among the great wonders of Lordaeron. Dignitaries travelled it to the capital, and after the First War Anduin Lothar led the refugees of Stormwind along it into the north. Now the Forsaken claim the forest, though the worgen of Shadowfang Keep, the Scourge and the wizards of Dalaran all dispute it.

entries.title: The Sepulcher
body: Once no more than a graveyard and an old crypt beside the road through Silverpine. After the Third War the enterprising Forsaken converted it into their base in the forest.
With the worgen to the south, the Scourge to the east and the Kirin Tor to the south-east, it is one of the only safe places in Silverpine for travellers of the Horde.

entries.title: Pyrewood Village
body: A Gilnean village of a town hall, a smithy and a chapel on the river below Shadowfang Keep. Like Ambermill it belonged to Lord Darius Crowley, and when King Greymane built his wall, it was left outside. When the Scourge came, the gates stayed shut. Some villagers sailed for Stormwind on a ship called the Sea Wolf and were never heard from again.

During the Third War, Prince Kael'thas and the night elves of Tyrande Whisperwind and Maiev Shadowsong made Pyrewood their last stop before the river, and held its bridge against a Scourge ambush until it collapsed under Tyrande.
Then Arugal cursed the villagers. By day they are human and still trade with Alliance travellers. At night they become the Moonrage worgen, and turn on everyone. Their ruling council serves Arugal.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Pyrewood Village (Origins, Third War and aftermath, The worgen curse)

entries.title: Shadowfang Keep
body: A keep on a high bluff overlooking Pyrewood, once named Silverlaine Keep. It was home to the lords of Pyrewood, who answered to the Crowley family. Baron Silverlaine ruled it, and his forces were led by Commander Springvale, a paladin of the Silver Hand.

When Arugal's worgen ran rampant through the forest, they overwhelmed the keep and killed the Baron and his household. Arugal retreated into it, named it Shadowfang Keep, and haunted by the ghosts of the dead lords, rules there over his worgen "children".

entries.title: Ambermill
body: A Gilnean lumber town south-west of Lordamere Lake, once Darius Crowley's, and of little importance before the Third War.

It sits on a dormant ley line node, and after the war the wizards of Dalaran, rebuilding their city, occupied it and set about reawakening the node for some great project. The Forsaken fear that if it succeeds they will lose their hold on Silverpine. To them Ambermill is the heart of human opposition in the forest.

entries.title: Deep Elem Mine
body: A mine in the middle of the forest. Arugal's curse spread to its miners, and the worgen made it their home, led by their cunning former foreman, Grimson the Pale.

entries.title: Beren's Peril and Olsen's Farthing
body: Olsen's Farthing was once a bustling farmstead right on the forest's trade road. Now it lies in ruins, and the undead of Thule Ravenclaw attack anyone who comes near.
In the hills south-west of Ambermill, at Beren's Peril, more of Ravenclaw's servants are hiding. Forsaken scouts believe they are preparing an attack on the Sepulcher.

entries.title: The Decrepit Ferry
body: Once a bustling ferry carried goods and people to Fenris Isle. The farms nearby sold their crops to the island's rich lord, and the ferryman was paid a small fee for each trip.
Then the Scourge came. The ferryman was brutally murdered, the ferry destroyed, and ghouls, skeletons and Rot Hide gnolls overran the docks.

entries.title: Fenris Isle
body: A large island in the middle of Lordamere Lake, forming a broken circle of land with the Dawning Isles. Before the Third War it held Fenris Keep, a thriving military outpost of Lordaeron.
When the Scourge took the land, the island's people fled or were murdered. The Rot Hide gnolls hold it now.

entries.title: Fenris Keep
body: The gloomy keep on Fenris Isle. It was of real strategic importance, and housed a sizable part of Lordaeron's army.
When the Scourge washed over Lordaeron, Thule Ravenclaw, an ambitious young mage of the Kirin Tor, allied himself with them, enslaved the local gnolls and made himself master of the keep.

entries.title: The Dead Field
body: A decrepit, abandoned farm in northern Silverpine. No one knows who lived there. Now it is a base for the Rot Hide gnolls, and their growing numbers suggest the Scourge is planning something.
Small Forsaken attacks on the field have all failed because of the banshee Nightlash, who appears whenever the gnolls under her command are attacked.

entries.title: The Ivar Patch and Malden's Orchard
body: Ivar's pumpkin patch was once a prosperous farm with many farmhands and servants. Ivar, his family and his workers all succumbed to the plague and became rotting ghouls that attack anyone who comes near.

Malden's Orchard, to the north-east, was abandoned when its owner fled the Scourge. Its dark evergreen trees have not been picked in years, and black worgs have taken over the orchard and its single small cottage.

entries.title: The Skittering Dark
body: An abandoned gold mine and its surroundings, now crawling with Skitterweb spiders, led by a giant matriarch hidden deep inside. Cocooned worgen, worgs, bears and orcs hang among the webs.

entries.title: Lordamere Lake
body: One of the largest lakes of the Eastern Kingdoms, rivalled only by Darrowmere. The human kingdoms of Lordaeron, Dalaran and Alterac all grew up around its shores, and it is most likely named, like the capital on its northern shore, after Lordain.

The Dawning Isles in its centre were once an idyllic chain of low keys; the plague sickened their trees, and murlocs and bog beasts roam them. After the battle at the ruins of Dalaran, Lady Vashj and her naga retreated here. Along the Shining Strand, the forest's lakeshore, the Vile Fin murlocs keep their villages.

entries.title: The Greymane Wall
body: A colossal wall with a great gate at the southern edge of Silverpine, raised by King Genn Greymane before the Third War, when Gilneas cut itself off from the Alliance in disputes over taxes for the orc internment camps and other quarrels.

It spared Gilneas the plague, but its gates stayed shut while refugees fleeing the Scourge camped and died outside. Inside, the wall bred civil war. Lord Darius Crowley, cut off from his lands in Silverpine, led the Northgate Rebellion, and Greymane crushed it. No word comes from Gilneas now.

entries.title: Valgan's Field and North Tide's Hollow
body: Valgan's Field, west of the Shining Strand, would once have been a lovely farm with a magnificent view of the lake. Its owner was killed or fled when the Scourge arrived. Arugal himself used to stay there in his Kirin Tor days.
The feral Moonrage worgen roam the deserted farms of the north. At North Tide's Hollow, just above the Sepulcher, they keep a crude camp with only what they need to survive.

entries.title: High Executor Hadrec
body: The Forsaken commander at the Sepulcher. He sends Deathstalker agents across northern Silverpine to judge the threat of the wildlife and the Scourge, and his investigation of the Rot Hide gnolls leads to Fenris Isle.

entries.title: Dalar Dawnweaver
body: A former archmage of the Kirin Tor, killed when the Scourge attacked Dalaran, raised to serve them, and freed by Sylvanas. He was there when Kel'Thuzad summoned Archimonde. He now serves the Forsaken at the Sepulcher.
He has nothing but contempt for Arugal, whom he calls a charlatan, a mage whose spellcraft was so feeble he propped it up with enchanted trinkets and was not fit to clean the chamber pots of Dalaran.

entries.title: Apothecary Renferrel
body: The Royal Apothecary Society's man at the Sepulcher, who collects the organs of the forest's corrupted creatures for the Society's research.

entries.title: Shadow Priest Allister
body: A Forsaken shadow priest at the Sepulcher who watches the south. To him, Ambermill and its Dalaran wizards are the source of human opposition in Silverpine, and its great project must not be allowed to finish.

entries.title: Rane and Quinn Yorick
body: Deathstalkers who, with Erland McKree, were sent to scout northern Silverpine. After passing the Dead Field they were ambushed by Ivar's ghouls, and Ivar himself wounded Quinn. The brothers barricaded themselves in Ivar's old house while Erland went on alone, only to be pinned by worgs in the cottage at Malden's Orchard.

entries.title: Thule Ravenclaw
body: A young mage of great promise before the Third War. With his friends Bethor Iceshard and Gunther Arcanus he wove a wand from their three apprentice wands as a symbol of their friendship.

The friendship ended when Thule willingly sold his soul to the Lich King. He came to hate the wand, but could not bear to part with it or let the others have it, so he stole it and hid it in Fenris Keep. He even turned on his bodyguard Alaric, giving the man's head to the gnolls, though Alaric lives on headless by Thule's necromancy.

entries.title: Arugal and the Worgen
body: Arugal was a patriot of Gilneas, a royal archmage and later a member of the Kirin Tor. When the Scourge reached the Greymane Wall, King Greymane asked him for a way to save the kingdom. Using the research of an old mage named Ur, and against the advice of the Kirin Tor, Arugal summoned the worgen, savage wolf-beasts sealed away for ages, though he warned the king of their ferocity.

The worgen broke the Scourge at the wall, then turned on the Gilnean soldiers, and their curse began to spread. Greymane abandoned Silverpine to contain it. Driven mad with guilt, Arugal adopted the worgen as his children and retreated to Shadowfang Keep, where he serves their leader, Alpha Prime, and spreads the curse through the forest.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Arugal (The Third War, World of Warcraft)

entries.title: The Rot Hides
body: The Rot Hide gnolls are Thule Ravenclaw's creation. He enslaved the gnolls of the lake country and pumps a necromantic ichor of his own making through their bodies, which gives them their unnatural vigour. From Fenris Keep he sends them and his spectral apparitions against the Forsaken.

entries.title: Silverpine in the Third War
body: The Scourge swept through the woods until the Greymane Wall stopped it. Their numbers kept growing, and fearing the wall would break, Genn Greymane opened the gate and sent his soldiers out. The Scourge defeated them and raised them as its own.

After the war, the largest band of Alliance survivors in Lordaeron gathered here under Grand Marshal Garithos, and Prince Kael'thas and his blood elves crossed the forest on their way to Dalaran. The night elves of Maiev and Tyrande came through hunting Illidan. Later Malfurion and Illidan, briefly allied, fought the Scourge in the woods to rescue Tyrande. It was here too that Sylvanas met the three dreadlords Balnazzar, Varimathras and Detheroc.
